# T7.03: can the CoreMedia plug-in signature check be neutralised to register our encoder system-wide? — No (in-place), and why

Follow-up to `T7.00-cli-and-extensions.md`, which concluded there is no supported way for a third party to
register a VideoToolbox **encoder** system-wide, and recorded "patching CoreMedia to skip the signature
check … is out." That decision was deliberately revisited (2026-10-18/19) and the direct-patch route was
investigated end to end on the Tahoe test VM (macOS 26.7.1, build **25G241**, x86_64). **Result: an in-place
patch of the dyld shared cache is infeasible on this build** — the kernel re-validates shared-cache pages by
hash at page-in, which is not relaxed by this driver's boot-args. The legitimate routes from T7.00
(per-tool injection, and an Apple Feedback request) stand unchanged.

Full reverse-engineering detail and the exact byte-level patch candidates live outside this repo, in the
gitignored analysis workspace (`rea-macos/coremedia-re/` and `rea-macos/tasks/reports/C1–C5`); per project
rules no Apple binaries or patched framework bytes are committed here.

## What the check is (reversed on 25G241)

VideoToolbox scans `/System/Library/Video/Plug-Ins`, `/Library/Video/Plug-Ins` and two `/AppleInternal`
folders and registers each as a search path in CoreMedia's encoder `FigRegistry`. When CoreMedia builds the
filtered result list, `figRegistryAddResultItem` validates each scanned bundle:

- The requirement is a **precompiled ~200-byte code-requirement (`csreq`) blob** held in CoreMedia's
  read-only `__TEXT.__const` — not a string parsed at runtime. It is the Apple-anchor requirement
  (`anchor apple` or Apple-platform-signed with a `com.apple.` identifier and the relevant leaf OIDs).
- It is evaluated once per bundle via `CFDataCreateWithBytesNoCopy` → `SecRequirementCreateWithData` →
  `SecStaticCodeCreateWithPath` → **`SecStaticCodeCheckValidity(code, kSecCSDoNotValidateResources, req)`**.
- **One gate only.** `SecStaticCodeCheckValidity` and the requirement blob each have exactly one reference in
  CoreMedia; the verdict is cached per scan-context; there is **no second check at encoder-open/`dlopen`**
  (VideoToolbox imports no code-signing validation APIs at all; loading the bundle executable is governed by
  dyld/AMFI, which this driver already relaxes).
- A built-in global (`_sDisableRegistryCodesignValidation`) can skip the check, but it is only set from a
  `CFPreferences` boolean **gated behind `os_variant_has_internal_content` (AppleInternal builds)** — never
  settable on a release build without also defeating that gate.

The "validate" decision traces to **VideoToolbox option bit 0**: VT adds each plug-in folder with an options
value whose bit 0 is set unconditionally, and CoreMedia stores `options & 1` as the per-item "needs
Apple-signature validation" flag. So the check can in principle be defeated from either side — rewrite the
CoreMedia requirement, clear the VT option bit, or neutralise the evaluator call — and all three were
reduced to exact, disassembly-verified byte edits (recorded in the gitignored workspace).

## Why none of them can be applied in place — the decisive result

On 25G241 the frameworks have **no on-disk binary**; the code lives only in the OS-cryptex dyld shared cache
(`/System/Volumes/Preboot/Cryptexes/OS/System/Library/dyld/dyld_shared_cache_x86_64h`). That cache file **is**
writable on this VM (the Preboot volume is not sealed; Authenticated Root and SIP filesystem protections are
disabled). Writing the patch to it, however, does not work:

- **Boot test:** after patching and rebooting, the kernel rejected cache pages during early boot
  (`CODE SIGNING: … rejecting invalid page … dyld_shared_cache_x86_64h`), SIGKILLed process after process,
  and panicked (`CS_KILLED initproc exited`). The VM would not reach a desktop.
- **Live test (no reboot, isolates the cause):** writing the same bytes into the cache file on the *running*
  system immediately produced `cs_invalid_page … denying page sending SIGKILL` on process after process
  (`parsecd`, `analyticsd`, `fontd`, …), cascading to the same `CS_KILLED initproc` panic — with **no reboot
  involved**. This rules out the reboot/reset path as the cause: it is the modified bytes themselves.

The diagnostic in every case is `cs_mtime == mtime`, i.e. the rejection is **not** an mtime/cache-freshness
trip — it is the **page content failing the cache's signed code-directory hash**. The kernel verifies
shared-cache pages by hash **at page-in, continuously**, and this path is **not** governed by
`amfi_get_out_of_my_way=0x1` / `amfi=0x80` (those relax AMFI's *who-signed* policy for loaded executables,
not the shared cache's page hashes). Authenticated-root being disabled is irrelevant — it covers the system
*volume* seal, not the cryptex cache's own code directory.

Consequently **every** in-place candidate (requirement rewrite, VT option-bit clear, evaluator neutralise)
fails identically: they all change bytes inside signed cache pages. Making an edited cache acceptable would
require re-signing the cache's code directory or installing a matching trust-cache entry — the code directory
is Apple-signed, so that is out of scope and not something this project will pursue or ship.

## Scope / safety of the investigation

- Done only on the dedicated Tahoe test VM. Every step was snapshot-first (`pre-coremedia`, `pre-c5`, plus the
  tooling's own pre-patch snapshot); each failed boot/live test was recovered by snapshot restore, verified by
  the cache's SHA-256 returning to the stock value and a clean boot with the stock 15 Apple encoders.
- No Apple binaries, cache images, or patched framework bytes are committed to this repo; they remain in the
  gitignored dev-VM workspace.

## Conclusion — updated "what NOT to do"

- **Do not patch the shared cache in place to bypass the CoreMedia plug-in signature check on 25G241.** It
  does not load our encoder — it SIGKILLs signed system processes as they page in the modified cache and
  panics the machine. This is a hard kernel page-in integrity check, independent of SIP/AMFI relaxation.
- The system-wide **bundle** route therefore remains closed by a mechanism below user space.
- **Supported / shipped routes are unchanged** and remain the answer:
  - **GUI apps:** the in-process Metal plug-in (`libnvencvt`), already shipped.
  - **CLI tools:** `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` injection (`nvenc-run`) — reaches every tool tested, touches no
    signed bytes.
  - **The real fix to request from Apple:** a MediaExtension **`MEVideoEncoder`** extension point (decoders
    have one; encoders do not) — the legitimate path for third-party hardware encoders to register
    out-of-process. User's to file.
- The only system-wide option that does **not** touch signed bytes — a launchd-wide injection/interposer —
  was left unimplemented; it is a global `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` and carries its own stability/scope
  trade-offs, to be weighed separately against simply shipping `nvenc-run`.
